title: A defender's resources: meet the chief threat, nothing more
outcomes: Names the chief threat before choosing a defensive move
Lists the defender's resources and picks the one that meets that threat
Notices when a resource that worked before no longer works after one change
Does not defend when nothing is threatened

steps.text: A defender has several resources: move the piece, defend it, block, capture the attacker, make a bigger threat, vacate a weak square before supporting it, give material back. 'Five ways to meet an attack' teaches the first five. The skill here is the order: **name the chief threat first**, then choose the resource that meets it, and nothing more.

steps.caption: White to move. Black threatens Qxg2 mate (the rook on g8 backs the queen up). The pawn steps to g3.

line.say: The pawn steps up to g3. g2 is no longer there to capture, and the pawn shuts the g-file in front of the king. The engine rates it best.
Black continues; the immediate threat has been met.

claims.statement: If White passes, Black mates with Qxg2.
g3 is the engine's best move.

steps.text:
**Vacate, then support.** *Rule of thumb:* if the piece standing on a weak square is itself the problem, move it first; supporting a square while the important piece still stands on it can leave both stuck.
**Over-defence.** If nothing is threatened, a defensive move is a lost move. Whichever resource you pick must stop the chief threat in the position as it is now.

steps.title: The same defence, one change
steps.prompt: In the first position the pawn move g6 meets the mate threat. Predict what happens when a white knight is added on g4 (look at what it blocks and what it threatens), and when the white queen is missing.
Think of the last time you were attacked in a game. Which threat did you name first, and which resource did you use? Was another resource available?
